newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends unchanged after intervention.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends unchanged after intervention.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar rebounded from early lows to close unchanged against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday following strong central bank defence against foreign speculation, dealers said.
The local dollar dipped as low as T$27.970, but ended at T$27.925, the same as Monday's T$27.925 close, on a late rebound triggered by heavy intervention in the last minute.
The intraday low of T$27.970 was well below an eight-year closing low of T$27.926 set on Wednesday, but was still higher than an eight-year intraday low of T$27.98 hit in May 1996.
Turnover through dealers was extremely heavy at US$470 million.
Dealers attributed the earlier slide to foreign investors' non-delivery forward buying on U.S. dollars, reflecting the strength of the greenback overseas.

"Foreign investors are actively conducting non-delivery forward buying on U.S. dollars because they think, with the Southeast Asian currencies plunging, the Taiwan dollar should also enter a downtrend," said one dealer.
Dealers said the central bank's intervention was a "must do" in order to keep the local rate stable.
"The central bank had to intervene, otherwise foreign investors would classify Taiwan as one of the Southeast Asian nations that could be easily influenced," said another dealer.
"The central bank's move has sent a strong signal that it would not easily let the Taiwan dollar fall simply because of speculation or anticipation," said a third dealer.
Dealers said specuation to seek a further downtrend would intensify if the local dollar continued to set eight-year lows.
For Wednesday, a T$27.90-94 range was seen.
